sections.title: Client code that talks to the server
sections.what: Defines the form a new case must have, lists the actions the app can take on cases, and provides one shared function that sends requests to the server. The exported caseService is what the rest of the app uses to read and change cases.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps all server calls in one place so pages do not each handle web requests and errors themselves.
sections.watch_out: The shared request helper reads the response as JSON before checking success, so a non-JSON error page shows a raw parsing error instead of the intended message.

summary: Client code that sends case requests to the server and returns the results to the app.
purpose: Gives the app one place to read and change cases, documents and processing through the server.
why: Likely reason: keeps web request details out of the individual pages.
how: First, the file defines the input shape for creating a case and the list of actions for cases. Then the shared request helper sends a request, returns nothing when the server says not found, and throws an error when the server reports a problem. The ApiCaseService class calls that helper for each action, and one shared instance is exported as caseService.
inputs: Case IDs, the display language, new case details (district, circle, village, khata, optional khesra, nickname), and fixture or document IDs.
outputs: Case details or document fixtures from the server, null when a case is not found, or an error.
risks: The request helper reads the body as JSON before checking success, so a non-JSON error response gives an unclear error. Only the case read sends the language header in the visible lines. Lines 4 to 6 are cut off, so some actions were not fully checked.
debug: If the app shows a generic request failure message, check the server response and status code for that case ID. A missing case should show as a 404 response. A parse error means the server sent something other than JSON.
